hook.line: You've been putting *lo*, *te* and *le* in front of the verb. With two verbs together, Spanish gives you a second place to put them, and you'll see both in every chat.
hook.en: I'm going to call you tomorrow.

rule:
With one verb, nothing changes: the little word goes in front. *Te llamo.*

With a verb plus a basic -ar, -er, -ir verb (*voy a llamar*, *quiero ver*, *puedo creer*), you choose:
in front of the first verb: *Te voy a llamar.*
glued onto the end of the second: *Voy a llamarte.*
Same meaning, both everyday Spanish.

The same goes for *estoy* + an -ando or -iendo verb: *Me estás escuchando* or *Estás escuchándome*. When you glue it onto -ando or -iendo, add an accent to keep the stress where it was: *escuchándome*, *leyéndola*.

The one place it can never go is between the two verbs: not *voy a te llamar*. And with *no*, the *no* stays in front: *No lo puedo creer*, *No puedo creerlo*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these unstressed object pronouns (*pronombres átonos*); glued to the end of a verb they are enclitic.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Voy a ___ mañana.* (*te llamar* or *llamarte*) I'm going to call you tomorrow.
yourTurn.why: It can't sit between the verbs, so it glues onto *llamar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right one and type it: *¿Me estás escuchando?* or *¿Estás me escuchando?* Are you listening to me? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: In front of the first verb is always safe: *¿Me estás…?*

yourTurn.prompt: I want to see you on Saturday. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te* goes in front of *quiero* or on the end of *ver*.

yourTurn.prompt: The contract? I'm going to read it tonight.
yourTurn.answer: ¿El contrato? Voy a leerlo esta noche.
accept: ¿El contrato? Lo voy a leer esta noche.
yourTurn.why: *El contrato* is a *lo* word, and *lo* can go in either place.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Can you help me?
yourTurn.why: Help me: *me* in front of *puedes*, or on the end of *ayudar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Move the little word to the end: *Lo voy a pensar.*
yourTurn.why: Glued onto the basic verb, same meaning.

yourTurn.prompt: Move the little word to the front: *No puedo creerlo.*
yourTurn.why: In front of the first verb, with *no* still leading.

yourTurn.prompt: Move the little word to the end: *Te estoy escuchando.*
yourTurn.why: On the end of an -ando verb, add the accent: *escuchándote*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. It goes in front of *voy* or on the end of *llamar*, never in between.
English says want to see you; Spanish glues *te* onto *ver*, or puts it before *quiero*.
Gluing a word on moves the stress, so *escuchándote* needs its accent.
On the end means one word: *llamarte*, no space.

personal: Write two plans for this week about people you know, one each way: *Voy a llamar…* with the little word glued on, and *Lo voy a…* or *La voy a…* with it in front.
